messages:
mara: Quick escalation - Vertex POC is blocked. SCIM requests return 403 'token not allowed for tenant', and SAML handshakes redirect to an internal RelayState URL. They said they rotated keys during our Dedicated cutover. Can someone triage?
evan: on it. paste the last few scim-proxy log lines + a redacted SAML assertion (NameID/Audience/RelayState). Also which API key string did they paste into the Dedicated console?
mara: logs (redacted):
```
scim-proxy: 403 forbidden - token audience mismatch (hosted-key cannot access tenant:vertex)
scim-proxy: upstream basepath mismatch: expected /dedicated/vertex, got /hosted
saml-service: Assertion Audience=\"https://app.vertex.internal/sso\" (expected https://redwood.example.com/saml/acs)
http: RelayState=https://internal.vertex.app/after-login
```
lee: sounds like the classic two-parter: hosted vs tenant key mismatch for SCIM, and the IdP app is using a generic RelayState pointing to their internal SPA. Also check region: tenant tokens are region-scoped.
mara: they pasted a short key 'rudx-1a2b3c' (hosted-style) into the Dedicated SCIM field and used the global scim path instead of the eu endpoint. They also noted their org SSO workflow requires RelayState to send users to a dynamic internal app URL.
evan: immediate mitigation: (1) issue a temporary tenant-scoped token (region-matched) so provisioning can continue; (2) recommend they create a dedicated SAML app for Redwood so RelayState isn't forced to internal URL; (3) we can also add a temporary mapping rule on our SAML endpoint to ignore RelayState for that app while they finish setup.
lee: creating temp token now: `rudx-tenant-eu-temp-vertex-4h` (sent via secure DM). Also advise them to set the SCIM base URL to `https://eu.scim.redwood.company/dedicated/vertex/Users`.
mara: shared curl test for them to validate from their network:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer rudx-tenant-eu-temp-vertex-4h" \
  https://eu.scim.redwood.company/dedicated/vertex/Users | jq .
```
evan: RelayState note: if their IdP always includes a RelayState, we can't rewrite it on their IdP side. Best practice: create a small IdP app just for Redwood that sets default RelayState to blank or our ACS. If they need post-login routing, use a query param that the internal app reads instead of RelayState.
mara: they tried the curl test -> 200 OK and user list returned. SCIM provisioning resumed. They updated SCIM connector to use tenant token and eu endpoint.
lee: SAML follow-up: sent metadata + recommended app config. Also proposed an interim SAML proxy toggle for onboarding: `--allow-override-relaystate` which will ignore the incoming RelayState and use our ACS for assertion validation. Infra review required.
onboard-bot: SCIM sync job 7712 completed: 143 users provisioned, 4 updated, 0 errors.
mara: Vertex created a dedicated SAML app and set ACS to our metadata URL; they also removed the internal RelayState. After re-testing SSO login succeeded.
infra-bot: follow-up created INFRA-799: add UI heuristic that warns when a hosted-style key is pasted into a tenant-scoped field and when the SCIM URL region doesn't match token region.
mara: customer confirmed POC access and SSO. closing. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
